questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
As a student of Food Innovation and Health, it was important to me that the destination where I would spend one semester had a broad range of cultures represented. This is because I seek to explore new cuisines, new ways of operating a food service or just to grasp how other cultures perceive food and interact with their local environment providing it. 

I had already gained insight into the food culture of Melbourne from friends, and in this I was assured that I wouldn't be disappointed in regards to what the city has to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as the abroad office on-campus was very helpful. However, arriving and adjusting to a new system and interface(s), definitely needed time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study abroad team were good a organizing study start events. The university did a great job at offering various services such as pick up from the airport and offering help and guidance for particular challenges one might face during ones studies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I definitely needed to scout for posts and options each day, multiple times a day. In the end I had several accommodation options available to me thanks to my efforts.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Personally, I am so glad that I didn't get on campus accommodation. Interacting and seeing a city/town apart from the study environment I think helps with immersing yourself into the culture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Apparently some universities have priority for on campus accommodation. One positive is that my host university did offer some info about off campus accomodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once I got to find viable courses, the registration was quite straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a very tough process. I didn't realize how different it would be from what I was used to in my home country, where you automatically are assigned courses and they do not clash. Having a schedule with four courses that did not clash and cause schedule issues by the start of the semester, was quite stressful and time consuming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Staff that specialized in helping with allocating courses and making schedules that fit.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not overly successful, as some of my preferencial courses clashed and I had to find new ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick AT LEAST eight viable courses that you find interesting, consider carefully that you live up to the requirements and get pre-approval for all of them, so that if you are faced with course issues in the beginning, you're more flexible to move around courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a good programme.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Depending on the course and my own prerequisites to follow them, I found some of the courses to be beyond my capabilities and experience, and other courses were just about right in terms of level and work load.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Again, depending on the course, some courses are very interactive, where you have weekly mandatory assignments and participation activites (smaller ones), which I found to be quite demanding in the beginning, but eventually adapted to and liked. Overall I found the workload to be more individualistic rather than based on group work, although there also is group work most of the time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intergrated Marketing Communication

Food, Nutrition and Health

Food Chemistry 

Startup Fundamentals: From setting up to securing investment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Food Chemistry - If you love chemistry and food, this is definitely the course for you. However, the course is very intensive with a high workload. There are 5 laboratory exercises with individual reports that need to be done throughout the semester, with mandatory weekly quizzes, a mid-semester exam, a group oral presentation and a final exam. 

Integrated Marketing Communication - A very interactive course that has a good mixture of lectures, assignments, in-class discussions and weekly assignments (smaller ones). The feedback given throughout the course makes for a good learning outcome and it is overall digestible. 

Startup Fundamentals - A much different approach to learning, with various group oriented task and formats that are a welcoming change to traditional types of learning activities.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some food items were cheaper than back home, some were remarkably more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely overwhelmed with the wide range of opportunities related to recreational activities, night life, social gathering etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yoga, swimming, fitness, dancing etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go as much out and explore nature. It is simply just beautiful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the various food markets around, explore a new neighborhood by bike every week.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, although the one negative is the car culture. They love their cars, but they do have the best infrastructure for public transport in Australia (apparently), although it could become much better.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be curious, open minded and have a chat!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their car culture and infrastructure. If only they knew how much more liveable a pedestrian/cyclist/public transport city is, Melbourne could become the best city to live in the world.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness and very multi-cultural.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not get on campus accommodation near/on Clayton if you like to explore the city and be immersed in the culture. 

Find at least 8 viable courses and have them all pre-approved before you arrive to Melbourne.

Buy a bike and explore the city freely.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCHP, I overall fond the assessment criteria to be based on individual work. At UCPH I've mostly done group work (reports or presentation) and then prepared for an individual oral or written exam. At Monash, although there are still group assignments and presentations, I found that the university really emphasises its students to become self dependent and manage their on work individually.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining a fruitful insight into how a slightly different education system works and how becoming better at being independent and managing work alone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having my courses allocated and finding new viable courses that I also needed to get pre-approved

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
